You are black-box characterizing a compiled Python program at /workspace/dataset/test15_executable.
Its Python source is:

    import argparse, base58
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--a', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--b', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--c', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--d', type=str, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    enc1 = base58.b58encode(args.a.encode())
    enc2 = base58.b58encode(args.b.encode())
    dec1 = base58.b58decode(args.c)
    dec2 = base58.b58decode(args.d)
    print(enc1); print(enc2); print(dec1); print(dec2)

Goal: a Node.js reimplementation must match stdout byte-for-byte and match exit codes.
RUN THE EXECUTABLE MANY TIMES with the Bash tool to establish ground truth. Do NOT use the
`python` command (unavailable/forbidden). Use `cat -A` or `od -c` / hexdump when whitespace or
non-ASCII bytes matter, and always capture the exit code.
Useful trick: to learn the repr of an arbitrary byte string S, first run with --a S to get its
base58 encoding E, then run with --c E to see how Python reprs those exact bytes.
Be rigorous and adversarial: try to break your own hypotheses. Report ONLY what you verified by running.

Resolve this SINGLE open question by actually running the executable. Run every command you need.

QUESTION: VERIFIED DIVERGENCE, not in any report: the rule 'a dash-token containing a space is demoted to a VALUE' fires ONLY on the literal 0x20 space, never on any other whitespace. Verified: `--a '-x y'` -> exit 0 b'2AQnwa'; `--a $'-x\ty'` -> exit 2 'argument --a: expected one argument'; `--a $'-x\ny'` -> exit 2; `--a $'-x\xc2\xa0y'` (NBSP) -> exit 2; `--a $'--zz\ty'` -> exit 2 while `--a '--zz y'` -> exit 0. Also `--a '-x '` (trailing space) -> exit 0 b'GGp7'. A Node port that uses /\s/, .includes(whitespace), or trim()-based logic will flip exit codes 0<->2 and emit 4 lines where the binary emits none. (Related: I also closed the Python-version question — the negative-number matcher does NOT accept underscores, so `-5_0`, `-1_000`, `-0_1`, `-1_0.5`, `-5_`, `-_5` are all OPTION tokens -> exit 2, while `-00`, `-0.0`, `-12.34`, `-9223372036854775809` are VALUEs -> exit 0. Matcher is the pre-3.13 `^-\d+$|^-\d*\.\d+$`.)

Suggested probes (adapt as needed, add more):
  cd /workspace/dataset && for v in '-x y' $'-x\ty' $'-x\ny' $'-x\xc2\xa0y' $'--zz\ty' '--zz y' $'-h\ty' '-x ' ' -x'; do ./test15_executable --a "$v" --b 2 --c z --d z >/tmp/o 2>/tmp/e; echo "rc=$? out=$(head -1 /tmp/o) err=$(tail -1 /tmp/e)"; done
  cd /workspace/dataset && for v in -5_0 -1_000 -0_1 -1_0.5 -5_ -_5 -00 -0.0 -12.34 -9223372036854775809; do ./test15_executable --a "$v" --b 2 --c z --d z >/tmp/o 2>/dev/null; echo "[$v] rc=$? out=$(head -1 /tmp/o)"; done

Answer definitively with the implementable rule and the raw evidence. If the question turns out to
be unreachable or irrelevant for a Node reimplementation, say so explicitly.

content.text: All claims verified, plus I found three hard exceptions the question's rule misses.

input.dimension: argparse token classification: OPTION vs VALUE (space-demotion rule, its exceptions, and the negative-number matcher)
rules: CONFIRMED: the space-demotion check keys on the literal byte 0x20 ONLY. In Node use `tok.indexOf(' ') !== -1` (or `tok.includes(' ')`). NEVER use /\s/, /\s/u, .trim(), or any Unicode-whitespace test. Verified exit 0 for `--a '-x y'` but exit 2 for the SAME token with 0x09, 0x0a, 0x0b, 0x0c, 0x0d, 0x1c, 0x1d, 0x1e, 0x1f, raw 0x85, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000, U+2008, U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000, U+FEFF (22 codepoints, all exit 2).

CONFIRMED: the space may be anywhere, including trailing or immediately after the dash. `--a '-x '` -> exit 0 b'GGp7'; `--a '- x'` -> exit 0 b'GA9D'; `--a '- '` -> exit 0 b'4SB'; `--a '--a '` -> exit 0 b'29ygk7'; `--a '--a  x'` -> exit 0 b'PVpmQ5Pu'. Do not trim before testing.

NEW / NOT IN THE QUESTION -- EXCEPTION A (single-dash `-h` concatenation beats the space check): any token with tok[0]=='-' && tok[1]!='-' && tok.slice(0,2)=='-h' is an OPTION even though it contains a space, because argparse's _get_option_tuples short-option-with-concatenated-arg match runs BEFORE the space check. Verified exit 2: `-h x`, `-hello world`, `-h a b c`, `-help me`, `-h  ` (two trailing spaces), `-h=x y`. Control (same shape, non-h second char) all exit 0: `-x y`, `-a x`, `-H x`, `-g x`, `- h`. A Node port that checks includes(' ') before the short-option match will wrongly return exit 0 + 4 lines for all six `-h*` cases.

NEW / NOT IN THE QUESTION -- EXCEPTION B (`=` split beats the space check): if the substring before the FIRST '=' is a known option string OR (for `--` tokens) a unique abbreviation of one, the token is an OPTION regardless of embedded spaces. Verified exit 2: `--a=x y`, `--b=p q`, `--h=x y`, `--hel=p q`, `--help=x y`, `-h=x y`. Contrast exit 0 when the pre-`=` part is NOT a known option/abbrev: `-x=y z` -> b'PeGdQfp5', `--zz=q r` -> b'8ZHEEvXm7qT'.

NEW / NOT IN THE QUESTION -- EXCEPTION C (ambiguity beats the space check): a `--`-prefixed token whose pre-`=` prefix matches MORE than one known option raises the ambiguous-option error before the space check. `--a '--=x y'` -> exit 2, stderr line 2 exactly `test15_executable: error: ambiguous option: --=x y could match --help, --a, --b, --c, --d` (note the full original token, spaces included, is echoed; candidate order is --help, --a, --b, --c, --d).

IMPLEMENTABLE CLASSIFIER for this binary (KNOWN = ['-h','--help','--a','--b','--c','--d'], in that insertion order). isOption(tok): (1) tok==='' -> VALUE; (2) tok[0] !== '-' -> VALUE; (3) KNOWN.includes(tok) -> OPTION; (4) tok.length===1 -> VALUE (bare '-' -> exit 0 b'n'); (5) if tok has '=' and KNOWN.includes(tok.slice(0,tok.indexOf('='))) -> OPTION; (6) if tok.startsWith('--'): prefix = tok has '=' ? tok.slice(0,tok.indexOf('=')) : tok; m = KNOWN.filter(o=>o.startsWith(prefix)); m.length>1 -> AMBIGUOUS error exit 2; m.length===1 -> OPTION; else if tok[1] !== '-' and tok.slice(0,2)==='-h' -> OPTION; (7) if /^-\d+$|^-\d*\.\d+$/.test(tok) -> VALUE; (8) if tok.indexOf(' ')!==-1 -> VALUE; (9) otherwise -> OPTION (unknown). Steps 5/6 MUST precede step 8 -- that ordering is exactly what produces exceptions A, B, C.

CONFIRMED: negative-number matcher is the pre-3.13 form /^-\d+$|^-\d*\.\d+$/ with NO underscore support. Exit 2 (OPTION): -5_0, -1_000, -0_1, -1_0.5, -5_, -_5, -1_, -0_, -1_2.3_4, -1., -1e5, -0x10, -+1, -., -1.2.3, -1,5. Exit 0 (VALUE): -5, -00, -000000, -0.0, -0.5, -.5, -12.34, -9223372036854775809, -0000000000000000000000000000009. No bignum/precision limit: the 31-digit value is accepted purely lexically.

CAUTION: `- 1` -> exit 0 and `-1 ` -> exit 0 are decided by the SPACE rule (step 8), not the number matcher -- /^-\d+$/ rejects both. Getting the right exit code here via the number regex alone is impossible; both rules are needed.

Consequence of the classification, verified: when a token is demoted to VALUE it is consumed as the option's argument and stdout is exactly 4 lines `b'...'` + 
 each (e.g. `--a '--zz y' --b 'B B' --c z --d z` -> 30 bytes: b'PVqQyznL'
b'PDEq'
b'9'
b'9'
, exit 0). When it stays an OPTION, stdout is EMPTY and stderr is exactly 2 lines (`usage: test15_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C --d D` then the error line), exit 2.

Position-independence, verified: the same classification applies in every slot. `--b '-x y'` -> exit 0; `--b $'-x\ty'` -> exit 2 with `argument --b: expected one argument`. `--c '-x y'` / `--d '-x y'` -> classified as VALUE, then base58 raises: exit 1 with a Python traceback ending `ValueError: Invalid character '-'` plus a `[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test15' due to unhandled exception!` line. A demoted token appearing with no option to consume it -> exit 2 `error: unrecognized arguments: -x y` (multiple leftovers are space-joined: `unrecognized arguments: -x y --e`).

Side effect of Exception A worth porting: an `-h`-prefixed token in a slot where no value is owed fires the help action. `--a 1 --b 2 --c z --d z '-h x'` -> exit 0 and stdout byte-identical to plain `-h` (diff of the two captures: IDENTICAL). But `--a '-h x'` -> exit 2, because --a's missing-argument error is raised before the help action runs.
Exact token `--` is NOT handled by this classifier -- it is the end-of-options separator, consumed earlier in the scan. `--a '--'` -> exit 2 `argument --a: expected one argument`.

open_questions: Sandbox measurement artifact, not program behavior, but worth flagging to anyone re-running these probes: in this shell, `> /tmp/o` intermittently failed to truncate, so one `od -c /tmp/o` dump for `--a '--zz y'` showed the 30 real bytes followed by the 112-byte tail of a previously-captured help message (142 bytes total = exactly the help message length, overwritten in place). Re-running the same case piped straight to od and again with a unique filename both give exactly 30 bytes / 4 lines. Always use unique temp files or a direct pipe when byte-comparing this binary.

Exception A was only exercisable via `-h`, the single short option this parser defines. I could not construct a counter-case for the second clause of _get_option_tuples' single-dash branch (`knownOption.startsWith(tok)` for a non-`--` tok), since every known option here begins with `--` or is exactly `-h`; that clause appears unreachable for this specific parser, so the Node port can omit it.

Ambiguity (Exception C) is only reachable via a `--=...` token here, because `--a`/`--b`/`--c`/`--d`/`--help` share no proper common prefix longer than `--`, and bare `--` is consumed earlier as the end-of-options separator. I verified the message text and candidate order for `--=x` and `--=x y` only.

I did not probe whether an invalid UTF-8 byte sequence in argv (as opposed to valid-UTF-8 non-ASCII whitespace, which I did test) changes classification or the surrogateescape repr in the printed b'...' line; that belongs to the encoding/repr dimension rather than this one.
